countries.summary: Sweden reduced the energy tax on electricity used in data centres from 2017. A 2022 Finance Ministry proposal (regeringen.se) removed that reduction from 1 July 2023, and the National Audit Office later criticised the decision basis. This pass found no binding Swedish heat-reuse mandate; the Stockholm district-heating operators' waste-heat arrangement is voluntary. Coverage is thin: Microsoft's Swedish sites and municipal pushback were not researched, and the 2023 enactment is not yet confirmed.

Finland moved electricity used by data centres from the reduced electricity tax class II to the general class I from 1 July 2026, with a planned ten-year tax relief for consumption in place of the reduction (government release, not read directly). DatacenterDynamics reports that a planned Google data centre was put on hold after the tax proposal. Microsoft's Espoo and Kirkkonummi campus is the leading heat-reuse case: waste heat feeds the Fortum district heating network, per a 2022 Microsoft announcement.

Microsoft's three Attica data centres (Spata-Artemida and Kropia, eastern Attica) were proposed for fast-track strategic-investment status in 2022 and carry a Government Gazette investment-incentive record. The Greek investment portal lists the project as Microsoft Operations 4733 Hellas. Public debate on energy and water demand exists in Greek press (To Vima), but this pass did not read those articles, so no water or energy claim is recorded.

fields.title: Data centres moved from electricity tax class II to the general class from 1 July 2026
fields.identifier: HE 156/2025 vp (government bill; per Bloomberg Tax and the Finnish government release)
fields.summary: Electricity used by data centres moves from the reduced tax class II to the general class I from 1 July 2026 (about 2.24 c/kWh under class I versus 0.05 c/kWh under class II, per a search summary of the government release). The change is expected to raise about EUR 47 million a year. A replacement state-aid scheme gives ten-year tax relief on consumption, capped at EUR 30 million in lost revenue, with timing reported as autumn 2026. Status is in_effect on the 2026-07-01 date per the IEA page as summarized; the scheme is not yet confirmed.

fields.name: Microsoft Finland datacentre region (Espoo / Kirkkonummi, Helsinki area), heat supplied to Fortum district heating
fields.notes: Announced 17 March 2022 as an intent to build a datacentre region in Southern Finland. Waste heat is to be converted to district heating with Fortum, supplying Espoo, Kauniainen and Kirkkonummi. Secondary coverage (search only) states the Espoo and Kirkkonummi data centres would eventually supply about 40% of the district heat needed in the area, while the 2022 release-era figure is 60%; the baselines differ, so neither is recorded. Construction and commissioning status were not confirmed in this pass. Google's Hamina heat-recovery project is NOT covered by this record.

fields.notes: Three data centres in two installation areas in Attica. Site 6 is 19.2 MW (Spata-Artemida); Sites 27 and 28 are 9.6 MW each (Kropia). power_mw is the sum of the three figures as printed, not a stated total. The Greek portal lists Government Gazette ΦΕΚ 3325 Β/28.6.2022, Interministerial Decision 74/2022, and an investment-incentive approval in ΦΕΚ 139 Β/10.1.2024. Status 'construction' comes from a search summary of Microsoft's October 2025 Greece fact sheet, which was not read (its PDF exceeded the fetch size limit), so it is unverified. Enterprise Greece's English page says the Board decided on 1 April 2022 to propose the project to the Interministerial Committee, and that it 'will create 300 new jobs within a decade'; the jobs figure is not recorded here because it is not first-party to a site claim. Microsoft's fact sheet (search only) says the Attica facility uses direct evaporative cooling and uses water for cooling less than 15% of the year; that is a first-party water claim and should be re-read and recorded as a claim once the PDF is fetched in part or in full.

fields.summary: Greece's Enterprise Greece board proposed the Microsoft Attica data-centre project to the Interministerial Committee on 1 April 2022 under the strategic-investment fast track, and the approval was published in the Government Gazette on 28 June 2022 as Interministerial Decision 74/2022. A later investment-incentive approval is recorded in ΦΕΚ 139 Β/10.1.2024. The instruments are incentive and fast-track approvals; they set no community-benefit or water or energy conditions that this pass found.
